_note: Hand fixes applied on top of the per-era research files.

facts: The AD 451 date marks the council, rather than an immediate complete institutional split.
Egyptian and Syrian opposition helped form lasting non-Chalcedonian churches.
Armenian rejection developed later.
Modern dialogues have found substantial agreement about Christ's divinity and humanity.

catholic.why: The largest Christian church, about 1.42 billion baptized members in 2024. Most Protestant traditions trace their separation from Rome to the Reformation.

anglican.sacraments: Two Gospel sacraments, baptism and the Eucharist. Baptism includes infants. Anglicans differ over counting five other rites and explain Christ's real presence in several ways.

pentecostal.sacraments: Usually two ordinances, believers' baptism and communion. Many distinguish Spirit baptism from conversion. Oneness churches link water and Spirit baptism to new birth. Some practice foot washing.

council-of-frankfurt.why: Frankfurt shows how disagreements over images and their translation strained relations between the Frankish and Byzantine churches. The later Frankish dispute over the Filioque was distinct from this council.
facts: Its first canon condemns Adoptionism, the claim that Christ is God's adopted Son in his humanity.
The Latin text wrongly made Nicaea II seem to demand for images the worship owed to God.
The Caroline Books, issued in Charlemagne's name, refuse both to smash images and to adore them.
Later, after the Frankish synod at Aachen in 809, Pope Leo III declined to add the Filioque to the creed.
council-of-frankfurt.disputed: Catholics and Orthodox both accept Nicaea II today. Historians debate how much bad translation, and how much rivalry with Byzantium, drove Frankfurt's rejection.

schleitheim-confession.why: The Swiss Brethren tied baptism to voluntary church membership and rejected violence, separating church life from political power.
facts: The gathering met on February 24, 1527.
Michael Sattler helped draft the articles.
These articles did not represent every Anabaptist group.
schleitheim-confession.disputed: The Swiss Brethren differed from both Catholic and magisterial Reformation churches over baptism and the use of coercion. Michael Sattler was executed at Rottenburg in May 1527.

lyon-ii.why: Lyon’s failed reunion shows why diplomatic agreement alone could not restore communion. Michael VIII’s profession of faith, prepared under Clement IV in 1267 and read at the council, also included a list of seven sacraments.
facts: Michael VIII’s profession of faith, read at the council, lists seven sacraments: baptism, confirmation, Eucharist, penance, orders, marriage and anointing of the sick.
The profession also affirms transubstantiation.
Emperor Michael VIII supports reunion partly for political protection.
Opposition in the Byzantine church prevents lasting union.
lyon-ii.disputed: Catholics recognize Lyon II as ecumenical. Eastern Orthodox churches reject its authority and the attempted union.

vatican-i.why: Resistance to the definitions helped form new Old Catholic churches in Germany and Switzerland. They later joined the older independent church of Utrecht, whose separation dated to 1723, in the Union of Utrecht (1889).
facts: The council opened in December 1869.
Pastor Aeternus defined papal infallibility on July 18, 1870.
Infallibility concerns defined teaching, not every papal statement or personal conduct.
War and Rome's capture interrupted the council in 1870.
vatican-i.disputed: Catholics call the definition a development of apostolic teaching. Old Catholics, Orthodox, and Protestants reject the claimed authority.

synod-of-dort.why: Calvinists and Arminians disagree about how God’s grace relates to human response. Dort established the position of churches subscribing to its Canons.
facts: Delegates met at Dordrecht in the Netherlands.
The Remonstrants followed Jacob Arminius's challenge to Reformed teaching.
The Canons address five disputed points, not all Christian doctrine.
synod-of-dort.disputed: Reformed churches accepted the Canons as faithful teaching. Remonstrants rejected the verdict and faced political suppression.

nicaea-ii.why: This council gives Orthodox and Catholic Christians a basis for honoring sacred images in prayer and liturgy.
facts: Empress Irene supports the council against opponents of religious images.
Honor shown to an image refers to the person depicted.
This is the last council both Catholics and Eastern Orthodox generally accept as ecumenical.
Further conflict ends with the Byzantine restoration of icons in 843.
nicaea-ii.disputed: Many Protestants reject or restrict honoring religious images. Catholics and Orthodox distinguish this honor from worship of God.

facts: The 869 to 870 council condemns Photius and confirms Ignatius, restored in 867, with papal legates presiding.
Canon 21 of the 869–870 council ranks the five patriarchal sees, with Rome first.
John VIII's legates join the 879 to 880 council, which recognizes Photius, who returned in 877, and forbids creed changes.
Some Orthodox writers call the 879 to 880 council the eighth ecumenical council.
disputed-eighth-council.disputed: The present Catholic and Orthodox receptions differ. The history of papal acceptance and the later numbering of these councils is more complex than a continuous division from 869 onward.

add.name: Eastern Catholic churches
add.summary: Eastern churches in communion with Rome, preserving their own worship and law. Brest in 1596 marks one reunion, not the beginning of all Eastern Catholic churches.
add.why: Catholic unity allows several Eastern rites, not only the Latin rite. Catholic and Orthodox churches still dispute the history of these unions.
facts: There are 23 Eastern Catholic churches alongside the Latin Church.
Maronites trace continuous communion with Rome. Other Eastern Catholic churches arose through reunions at different dates.
Many of them ordain married men as priests.
Each uses an Eastern rite such as Byzantine, Syriac, or Coptic.
add.sacraments: Seven sacraments, often called holy mysteries. Eastern tradition joins baptism, chrismation, and communion, including for infants. Practices differ across churches. Byzantine churches use leavened Eucharistic bread.
add.today: About 18 million in CNEWA's 2017 Annuario Pontificio figures
add.disputed: The 1993 Balamand dialogue rejected uniatism as a model for reunion, while affirming Eastern Catholic churches' right to exist.
